Cube Clubhouse® Privacy Policy

For Cube Clubhouse on iPhone and iPad, version 1.0. This is the same text the app shows on its Privacy page.

This version of Cube Clubhouse (1.0) collects nothing about the people who use it and sends nothing about them anywhere. There are no accounts, no adverts, no analytics, no purchases and no tracking of any kind.

What is saved, and where

Five small things are kept on your device, inside the app, so the app is where you left it:

  • which lessons have been practised, their stars, and the 🧠 badge for any finished without hints;
  • the cube size last chosen on the Play screen;
  • the speed chosen for the guided solve;
  • the times from the Timer screen, so it can show your best: each time with its cube size and any +2 or DNF, plus the cube size last chosen there and whether 15 Seconds to Look First is switched on. No dates, no names.
  • for the update check: whether it is switched on, the date it last asked the App Store, and a version you tapped Not Now for, so it does not ask again that week.

That is all of it. No names, no ages, no messages, no photos, no location, no identifiers. The app sends none of it anywhere and shares none of it between devices. The one way a copy leaves your device is inside your own backup of it — iCloud Backup, or a backup on your computer — if you make one. That backup belongs to your account; we never see it, and restoring it to a new device brings the stars along. Deleting the app, or tapping Clear Saved Progress on the app's About page, erases what is on your device; an older backup keeps whatever it held when it was made, until you delete that backup.

What the app asks the internet for

One question, to Apple, and you can switch it off. About once a day the app asks Apple's App Store whether a newer version of Cube Clubhouse is out, so it can offer the update. The question carries only the app's App Store name (its bundle identifier) and your device’s country or region, so it asks the right store. It carries nothing about the person using the app: no name, no progress, no times, and no identifier of anyone or of your device. Like any request on the internet it reaches Apple from your network's address; it never reaches us. Switch it off under About › Updates. Nothing else is ever requested, not even the typeface, which is stored inside the app like the lessons are. You can turn on Aeroplane Mode before anyone opens it and every part of the app still works; only the update check waits for a connection.

We did not simply leave the requests out; the app is built to block them. The page carries a rule that forbids it from loading anything from the web, and on iPhone and iPad the app tells the system to refuse any web address on its behalf as well. The update check is made by the app itself, not by the page, and goes only to Apple. If a later version ever changes what the app does with information, we will update this page first.

Nothing to buy

Cube Clubhouse is free to use and has no purchases, no subscriptions and no adverts, so there is no payment for anyone to handle — no card details, no billing address, no account, nothing at all of that kind passing through the app.

Reading aloud

The Read buttons use the voice built into your device, and only ever read the app's own instructions. On iPad and iPhone that voice runs on the device itself.

What the app never touches

No camera, microphone, location, contacts, photos or notifications. No cookies. No third-party code and no third-party servers: the one outside ingredient is the typeface, which is an open-source file stored inside the app and talks to nobody. The only server the app ever talks to is Apple's App Store, for the update check. The app does not show anything you do in it to anyone else.

Who we are, and how to reach us

Cube Clubhouse is made by Ira Learning LLC. For any question about privacy, about this page, or about the app itself, email us at support@iralearningllc.com.

A note for children using the app: if you would like to tell us something, please ask your parent or guardian to send the email for you, from their own email address, rather than sending it yourself.

If you write to us

An email is the one thing that ever reaches us, and only if you choose to send one. Only Ira Learning LLC reads the mailbox, which is protected with a strong password and two-step verification. We use your message only to answer it. We never add your address, or anyone's, to a mailing list or any other list, and we never share it.

If a child writes to us, we reply once, asking a grown-up to write instead, and then delete the message and the address.

How long we keep information

  • On your device: the stars, choices and times listed above stay until you tap Clear Saved Progress or delete the app; the update check's settings stay until you delete the app. We never receive any of it.
  • A grown-up's email: kept while we help, in case you write back, then deleted no later than 12 months after your last message. Ask us and we will delete it sooner.
  • A child's email: answered once, then deleted no later than 7 days after it arrives.

Children's privacy

Cube Clubhouse is made for a general audience of all ages, and some of the people who use it will be children, so we treat everyone as possibly a child. Because nothing is collected from anyone, there is nothing to consent to, nothing to request and nothing for us to delete — it is all on your device, and in your own backup of it if you make one, under your control. Our COPPA Review checks this against the US children's privacy law, rule by rule.
